concerns.text: FR-011 (processed_alloys.csv schema validation) lacks a story reference; no US mentions this artifact.
FR-012 (features.csv schema validation) is orphaned – no user story ties to this requirement.
FR-013 (sensitivity_report.json schema validation) is orphaned and duplicates FR-015.
FR-014 (feature_importance.csv schema validation) is not linked to any user story.
FR-015 (sensitivity_report.json schema validation) duplicates FR-013 and has no story anchor.
FR-013 and FR-015 are near‑identical (≈81% word overlap); they should be collapsed or differentiated.

FR-013 and FR-015 duplicate the same requirement (81% word overlap). Both state that `sensitivity_report.json` must conform to the schema defined in `contracts/sensitivity.schema.yaml`. This violates the scope rule that each functional requirement must be unique.

The idea only requests thermodynamic mixing parameters (enthalpy, atomic size mismatch). The spec adds a third descriptor, `electronegativity_variance`, which was not part of the original research question and expands the scope beyond what was asked.

The specification mandates a collinearity sensitivity analysis (flagging predictor pairs with |r| > 0.8 and re‑training). The original idea did not require this analysis, so this adds extra work not needed to answer the research question.

new_concerns.text: Constitution Principle VI mandates that thermodynamic descriptors include mixing enthalpy, atomic size difference **and** electronegativity variance. The current specification (FR‑001, FR‑002) only requires mixing enthalpy and atomic size mismatch, omitting electronegativity variance, thus violating the project constitution.
